title: GTA 6 Pre-orders Show Strong Demand for Ultimate Edition
description: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick reveals that many players pre-ordering GTA 6 are opting for the higher-priced Ultimate edition over the standard version.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Pre-orders Lean Toward the Ultimate Edition

The pricing and sales strategy for Rockstar Games' highly anticipated *Grand Theft Auto 6* continues to generate significant industry discussion. According to a recent report by Eurogamer, Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar's parent company Take-Two, has shed light on player purchasing habits regarding the game's pre-orders.

While the idea of paying triple-digit prices for a single video game can cause hesitation among some consumers, Zelnick revealed that a substantial portion of those who have pre-ordered *GTA 6* chose the more expensive Ultimate edition rather than the standard $80 (£70) version.

## Pricing Tiers and Consumer Choices

Prior to this, discussions surrounding a potential $100 price point for top-tier editions sparked widespread debate across the gaming community. With the Standard edition priced at $80 (£70) and the Ultimate edition reaching around $100 (£90), the market is showing a clear appetite for the premium offering among early adopters.

This trend suggests that dedicated fans are willing to invest more for the ultimate package, defying assumptions that higher price tiers would universally deter pre-order momentum for mega-hits.

## Implications for the Industry

This insight from Take-Two's leadership highlights the shifting economics of modern AAA game development. As budgets rise, the success of higher-priced special editions could encourage other publishers to experiment further with premium pricing tiers. Whether this trend will hold true across the broader consumer base upon release remains to be seen, but the early signals point to robust financial health for the title's launch.

## Editor's Take

Strauss Zelnick's comments highlight the sheer pulling power of the *GTA* franchise. The willingness of fans to snap up the $100 Ultimate edition shows that for true blockbusters, price resistance is often outweighed by anticipation. It's a strong indicator of Take-Two's lucrative path ahead.
